title: The Last Sigil Anew
premise: Silas Oyelaran, a royal food-taster whose body has become a ledger of poisons, secretly keeps accounts for the Guild of Impossible Things—a found family of gift-bearers who trade in miracles. When the crown declares the Purging Hunt and the guild's safehouse burns, Silas discovers the king is not cruel but bound: a sigil-crown feeds on his will, and it was forged from the last living dragon-fire. With Wren, a runaway hunt-captain who loves him against her oath, Silas must reach the dragon's dying ember beneath the palace and unbind the king before the fire—and every gift in the realm—gutters out forever. In the end, Silas spends his own poisoned immunity as the unbinding price, the king wakes free, and the guild becomes something new: not traders in impossible things, but keepers of them.
about_author: Zephyrine Thackeray is a former apothecary's apprentice turned archivist who claims she learned to write fiction by cataloguing other people's lies. She lives above a disused tannery with three cats named after failed treaties.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At a royal banquet, Silas tastes poison meant for the king and survives by habit; that night he updates the guild's ledgers, trading a bottled memory for bread. We meet the guild-as-family through small rituals. Emotional beat: warmth laced with dread—the first proclamation posters appear on the walls.

chapters.title: A Hunt Proclaimed
chapters.summary: POV Wren. A young hunt-captain reads the Purging decree aloud to her squad and feels her oath curdle—her own sister bears a gift. Ordered to raid a suspected safehouse, she hesitates one breath too long. Emotional beat: duty cracking under conscience; ends with her burning her orders instead of delivering them.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The guild debates whether to flee or fight; Grandmother Ash, its blind founder, reveals the crown on the king's head is a sigil fed by dragon-fire, and the fire is dying. Silas realizes his immunity ledger may be the key to an unbinding rite. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into fragile purpose.

chapters.title: The Captain Who Burned Her Orders
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Branded a traitor, Wren seeks the guild for sanctuary and collides with Silas mid-heist of the palace archives. Their escape through cisterns sparks wary trust—and an unmistakable pull between them. Emotional beat: two people built for duty discovering they'd rather be built for each other.

chapters.title: What the Poison Taught Me
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Flashback-woven chapter: how each poison Silas survived left a 'mark' in him, making his blood a map of the sigil's workings. The guild tests his blood against Ash's fragmentary rite—it fits, but the unbinding demands a life willingly given. Emotional beat: quiet horror; love against duty sharpens into a choice he hides from Wren.

chapters.title: The Ember Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Guided by Ash, the party descends beneath the palace and finds the last dragon—not dead but guttering, its fire siphoned into the crown for thirty years. The dragon names its price: the sigil can only be cut by one who has swallowed death and lived. Emotional beat: awe and grief; the found family vows to stand together even knowing what it costs.

chapters.title: Crownfall
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The guild infiltrates the coronation-anniversary masque. Wren holds the door against her former squad while Silas reaches the throne—only to find the king awake inside his binding, begging to be freed, and the crown's keeper, Lord Vessic, waiting with drawn steel. Emotional beat: betrayal at the threshold; everything hinges now.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Climax. Silas begins the rite as Vessic tries to feed the crown harder; Wren breaks her final oath to shield him; the guild pours their gifts into the working. Silas offers his poisoned, marked blood—and the dragon's last flame answers. The sigil shatters; Vessic, fused to its shadow, crumbles. Emotional beat: sacrifice made real, love declared in the fire.

chapters.title: Ashes and Accounts
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The king, freed and hollowed, must face what was done in his name; he pardons the gifted and dissolves the Hunt. Silas survives—but emptied of his immunity, ordinary for the first time. Wren chooses him over reinstatement. Emotional beat: tender aftermath, grief braided with relief.

chapters.title: Keepers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Silas (closing). A season later, the guild reopens its ledgers under a new name, teaching gifts instead of trading them; the dragon's ember, tended freely, begins to grow again. Silas writes the final entry—an account of debts repaid in love. Emotional beat: resolution and hope; found family as the truest magic remaining.
